findings.title: Earlier c.req.text()/json() followed by parseBody() on multipart now silently corrupts binary file parts instead of failing
findings.suggested_fix: When the arrayBuffer is being reconstructed from a non-binary cache (text/json), either fall back to raw request.formData() semantics (throw) or document that multipart bodies must not be read as text first. Alternatively cache arrayBuffer first in a middleware that needs the body.
findings.why_it_matters: parseFormData now goes through HonoRequest.arrayBuffer() (the #cachedBody fallback chain) rather than formData(). If any middleware previously called c.req.text() (logger, signature check), the arrayBuffer is rebuilt from the UTF-8-decoded text, and the real multipart Content-Type is then re-applied by bufferToFormData, so parsing 'succeeds' with mangled binary file bytes. Before the change this path threw (500) because new Response(text) carried a text/plain Content-Type.
evidence: app.post: await c.req.text(); then await c.req.parseBody() with a multipart upload of a file with bytes ff fe 80 81 00 90
New code: bodyCache={text}; request.arrayBuffer() -> new Response(text).arrayBuffer(); bufferToFormData(buf, original multipart CT) parses fine
Ran scratch repro: file length 6 became 16 and first bytes 239,191,189 (U+FFFD) with HTTP 200
Ran same repro against merge-base source: TypeError 'Content-Type was not one of multipart/form-data...' -> 500

findings.title: method-override middleware still gates on case-sensitive startsWith, so mixed-case Content-Type is still skipped
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the media type (split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()) in method-override like parseBody does, or share a helper.
findings.why_it_matters: Same bug class as #5060 remains in a sibling consumer of form bodies: a client sending 'Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded' with _method=DELETE is never overridden, so the request hits the wrong handler, even though parseBody/validator now accept that header. Inconsistent behavior across Hono components.
evidence: Request with Content-Type 'Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=...' and field _method=DELETE
contentType?.startsWith('multipart/form-data') is false -> falls through to next() without override; same for urlencoded at line 92

findings.title: validator regexes remain stricter than parseBody: OWS before ';' still yields empty {}
findings.suggested_fix: Make validator use the same media-type extraction as parseBody (split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase() compared to exact types) instead of whole-header regexes, or allow \s* before ';'.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix makes parseBody and validator agree on case but not on other Content-Type tolerance. Scratch run: header 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded ;charset=UTF-8' (and multipart with ' ;') parses via parseBody but validator('form') passes {} to the validation function. multipartRegex also rejects extra params before boundary (e.g. charset). Same silent-skip symptom as the original issue for other legal header shapes.
evidence: POST with content-type 'multipart/form-data; boundary=X' modified to 'multipart/form-data ; boundary=X'
/twice route (parseBody) returned the parsed fields; /ws route (validator('form')) returned {}

residual_risks: parseBody on HonoRequest now retains both bodyCache.arrayBuffer and bodyCache.formData (previously only formData, which was streamed by the runtime), roughly doubling retained memory for large uploads for the request lifetime.

Plain Request objects with an overridden/mocked formData() (custom subclasses, test doubles) are now bypassed by parseBody, which always reads arrayBuffer(); the removed vi.spyOn(req,'formData') mock in body.test.ts no longer exercises that path.

A malformed multipart body still surfaces as an uncaught TypeError (500) from parseBody, while validator('form') maps it to 400; and a rejected promise cached in bodyCache.formData by parseBody would make a later validator('form') await throw an unwrapped TypeError outside its try/catch (pre-existing shape, unchanged).

Verified no regression: second parseBody on HonoRequest, parseBody then c.req.text()/formData(), validator('form') then parseBody, cloneRawRequest after parseBody (now cache key is arrayBuffer first, which actually fixes a boundary mismatch), boundary case preserved, plain Request second call fails as before.
testing_gaps: No test for calling c.req.parseBody() twice or parseBody then c.req.formData()/text() on a HonoRequest with the new bodyCache.formData assignment.
No test combining parseBody and validator('form') in one route with a mixed-case Content-Type.
No test for method-override or other consumers with mixed-case Content-Type; no test for OWS before ';' in validator.
No test that a prior c.req.text() read followed by parseBody on multipart behaves sanely.
